title: Any Time, Any Space: A World-State-Centric Framework for Agentic Video Generation
abstract: ATAS improves long-form video consistency by compiling screenplays into referenced shot requests, retrieving spatial and temporal evidence from scene and event memories, and conditionally updating memory after generation.

title: Beyond Domain-Routed Supervision: Cross-Teacher Guarding for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
abstract: Road MOPD reduces gradient conflicts in multi-teacher distillation by using cross-teacher agreement for token-level credit assignment and auxiliary gradients to constrain conflicting updates.

title: Player-1: Learning to Play from Synthetic Experience
abstract: Player-1 improves game control by combining supervised fine-tuning on gameplay trajectories with reinforcement learning across synthetic environments, achieving substantial gains over demonstration-only baselines.

title: Doc2Harness: Benchmarking LLMs on Long-Horizon Harness Engineering of Coding Agents
abstract: Doc2Harness is a deterministic two-stage benchmark that evaluates long-horizon harness engineering by having models build and run harnesses across isolated containers, revealing substantial performance gaps among frontier models.

title: More Methods, Better Agents? A Reality Check on Self-Distillation in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Researchers benchmarked ten self-distillation methods against GRPO across multiple agent tasks and model sizes, finding limited consistent gains, hidden training instability, and no reliable cost-to-performance benefit.

title: Recovering Reliable Supervision via Critique-Guided On-Policy Distillation
abstract: CriticOPD improves on-policy distillation by using teacher critiques to restore recoverability, enabling students to revise incorrect reasoning and achieve stronger mathematical reasoning performance.

title: LatentLoop: Scaling Looped MoE Models with Asymmetric Compute Allocation
abstract: LatentLoop improves looped Mixture-of-Experts by compressing the first loop visit, reallocating saved computation to larger hidden dimensions, and using separate attention parameters, yielding lower validation loss and better benchmark scores.

title: Cortex: Consolidating Context into Parametric Memory
abstract: Cortex consolidates context-induced improvements into mergeable low-rank or structural updates, preserving non-target capabilities across sequential edits and diverse model scales.

title: ActionOPD: Distilling Decisions, Not Tokens
abstract: ActionOPD aligns smaller language-model agents with teachers via semantic action-level on-policy distillation, improving out-of-distribution tool-use performance without requiring shared tokenizers or teacher probabilities.

title: Seeing, Maintaining, and Learning: The Evolution of Multimodal Agent Memory
abstract: This work proposes a two-axis framework for multimodal agent memory covering information formation and adaptive management to support lifelong learning.

title: LensErase: A Foundation Model for Erase Anything
abstract: LensErase is a mask-based erasure foundation model pretrained on a large paired dataset and refined with reinforcement learning to handle diverse real-world removal tasks while preserving surrounding content.

title: KV4-RL: Unlocking Faster Asynchronous Rollouts for RLVR with INT4 KV Cache Quantization
abstract: KV4-RL accelerates reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards via INT4 KV cache quantization with selective INT8 protection, achieving substantial speedups with minimal accuracy loss.

title: Towards Agentic Robots: Model, Data, Environment, and Harness
abstract: This survey unifies research on agentic robots by tracing the evolution from robot policies to integrated systems using vision-language-action models, world models, and structured functional domains.

title: Many Right Answers, One Training Example: Removing Responder Noise from GRPO for LLM Recommenders
abstract: ReMaRk improves reinforcement learning for recommendation by scoring generated lists against all valid replies jointly, reducing training cost while matching or exceeding prior performance.

title: CLASHarness: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Conflict in Computer Use via a Controllable and Verifiable Generation Pipeline
abstract: CLASHarness introduces a controllable framework for generating verifiable multi-agent conflicts in computer-use tasks, revealing that frontier vision-language models struggle with verifying ground truth, resolving conflicts, and coordinating shared resources.

title: The Thinking Leakage in Reinforcement Learning for LLMs
abstract: Reinforcement learning gains in hybrid reasoning models' NO-THINK mode largely stem from reactivating existing THINK-mode reasoning rather than learning new capabilities.

title: RuleTrek: Benchmarking Agentic Rule Reasoning in Complex Scenarios
abstract: RuleTrek is a multi-domain benchmark that evaluates large language model agents on identifying, deducing, and applying domain-specific rules across complex, multi-file scenarios, revealing substantial performance gaps.

title: Super-Resolution in The Right Latent Space: A Frozen Vision-Foundation Substrate
abstract: Real-world super-resolution is improved by mapping degraded image embeddings back to a high-resolution manifold within a frozen DINOv3-L latent space, yielding high fidelity and fast inference.

title: HumanoidToolBench: Benchmarking Humanoid Tool Use from Selection to Mobile Execution
abstract: HumanoidToolBench evaluates humanoid robots on tool selection and coordinated manipulation and locomotion across diverse tasks, revealing gaps between selection and execution.

title: APT: Feedback-Driven Agentic Post-Training for Text-to-Image Generation
abstract: APT is an automated framework that adaptively post-trains text-to-image models by using agents to evaluate capabilities, diagnose failures, and generate targeted reinforcement learning data in a self-improving loop.

title: DecisionRobust: Benchmarking Robustness for JEV Style Decision Models Across Text and Vision
abstract: DecisionRobust evaluates decision model reliability against adversarial text, image, and prompt injection attacks, showing that robustness varies by task and that label consistency checks reduce apparent attack success.

title: LabInstruct: Benchmarking Situated Instructional Video Generation for Lab Procedures
abstract: LabInstruct evaluates AI-generated instructional videos for real laboratory tasks and reveals that visual plausibility does not ensure procedural correctness.

title: SwarmRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Evolving Scientific Agent Swarm
abstract: SwarmRSI evolves scientific agent swarms through feedback-guided mutation and complementary recombination to enable recursive self-improvement across research tasks.

title: τ-Emotion-Bench: Exposing the Interaction Fragility of LLM Agents through Real-World User Emotions
abstract: A benchmark and data pipeline evaluate and improve LLM tool-calling agents under emotionally varied user interactions by filtering ineffective trajectories and scaling supervised training.

title: SkillMarker: A KGW-Based Watermarking Method for Agent Skill Ownership Verification
abstract: SkillMarker embeds watermarks into agent skills while preserving instruction accuracy to enable ownership verification and leakage tracing.

title: RAR: Rate-Adaptive Rollout for Time-Consistent Interactive World Models
abstract: Rate-Adaptive Rollout enables interactive world models to generate video at variable temporal rates with consistent dynamics and extended physical horizons.

title: ProgAgent: Learning Tool Orchestration through Programmatic Training
abstract: ProgAgent introduces a programmatic tool-calling training framework that improves long-horizon agent performance by using executable code and runtime variables instead of sequential context accumulation.

title: GroundGUI: GUI Grounding by High-Quality Data and Distillation-to-Reinforcement Learning
abstract: ScreenRef provides multimodal GUI grounding annotations across desktop, web, and mobile environments, and the D2RL training approach improves model generalization to achieve state-of-the-art results among 8B-scale agents.

title: Apertus 1.5: From Open Text Models to Open Multimodal Reasoners
abstract: Apertus 1.5 extends open multimodal language models to image and audio reasoning with long-context training, reinforcement learning, and fully open data and weights.

title: Efficient Scene-Text Refinement via Pixel-Space Grouped Image Generation
abstract: PixText refines local text in generated images via grouped pixel-space generation with MeanFlow, improving glyph accuracy while preserving backgrounds and reducing inference cost.

title: Are We Testing Too Much? A Survey of Benchmark Compression for Efficient Evaluation of Large Language Models
abstract: This survey organizes benchmark compression methods for large language models into a taxonomy covering subset selection, cross-suite recovery, and adaptive evaluation to reduce evaluation costs while maintaining reliability.

title: APEX-Harm: Evaluating Agent Safety in Shared Professional Workspaces
abstract: APEX-Harm evaluates long-horizon agent vulnerabilities to injection attacks across large multi-tool workspaces, revealing high success rates for script-based attacks despite correct task outputs.

title: Diagnosing and Correcting Reward Hacking in Verifiable Instruction Following
abstract: CALIF combines verifier rewards with a calibrated likelihood bonus to prevent reward hacking and maintain response quality during reinforcement learning on instruction-following benchmarks.

title: Long-Horizon RL Needs Muon
abstract: A single-rollout asynchronous training recipe combining Muon optimization, token-averaged loss, truncated importance sampling, and auxiliary penalties improves long-horizon agent success on repository-level issue resolution.

title: LLM-to-Flow Distillation: Teaching Natural Language Goals to Scientific Generators
abstract: LLM-to-Flow Distillation aligns scientific generators with high-level discovery goals by using a frozen LLM to build adaptive curricula and distill preferences via DPO, enabling control over peptide and small-molecule design.

title: Joint Subspace Sparse Attention for Efficient Long-Context Decoding
abstract: Joint Subspace Sparse Attention improves long-context decoding by learning a shared low-dimensional query-key subspace for accurate token selection and using a gather-free kernel, achieving near-full accuracy with substantially higher throughput.

title: SafeDriveVLA: Navigation-Conditioned World Model Dreaming for Conflict-Aware End-to-End Autonomous Driving
abstract: SafeDriveVLA improves autonomous driving by predicting navigation compliance and using world-model dreaming to avoid unsafe instructions, outperforming existing vision-language-action models.

title: Share the Symbol, Not the Vector: Training-Free Fact Communication Across Language Models
abstract: SYNC enables heterogeneous language models to share selective object facts via word indices and receiver-local hidden-state directions without fine-tuning or translators.

title: What Makes a Social Agent's Interactions Effective? Learning from Verifiable Outcomes in Paired Worlds
abstract: HICO-Bench evaluates whether conversational agents produce feasible, verifiable coordination plans, and PaCPO improves success by rewarding turns that yield correct tentative plans across paired scenarios.

title: From Failures to Learnable Worlds: Policy-Conditioned Environment Generation for Navigation Agents
abstract: WEDGE guides environment generation for embodied navigation agents by diagnosing policy failure modes and constructing targeted training scenarios that address specific weaknesses.

title: Rethinking Projector Training in Multimodal LLMs
abstract: PORTAL initializes multimodal projectors without paired data by aligning vision and language feature distributions via optimal transport, matching standard training performance while eliminating projector training.

title: StartLux-Decision: AutoThink Decision Models with Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Deliberative Decisions
abstract: StartLux-Decision introduces efficient and adaptive decision models using single-pass prediction and confidence-guided reasoning, trained via a three-stage pipeline with RLCD² reinforcement learning, and evaluates them on Decision Index and the DecisionPivot benchmark.

title: Glance Forcing: Making Bidirectional Diffusion Autoregressive at a Glance
abstract: Glance Forcing improves video generation efficiency by splitting denoising into specialized experts guided by stage-specific objectives, reducing training costs while improving quality.

title: ProbabilityBench: Model Evaluation and Calibration with Exact Ground-Truth Uncertainty
abstract: ProbabilityBench supplies exact instance-level class probabilities across simulated text domains to directly evaluate model calibration and benchmark standard metrics against known ground truth.

title: BigCell: Generating Gigapixel Whole-Slide Images
abstract: BigCell generates coherent gigapixel-scale histopathology images using flow-matching transformers and adaptive scheduling, enabling text-conditioned synthesis and improving few-shot classification.

title: VITAL: From Visual Motion to Precise Action
abstract: VITAL derives driving actions from visual motion via a coupled motion scaffold and residual tokenizer, enabling fast, accurate trajectory prediction and bounded reinforcement refinement.

title: TextVerifier: Seeing Beyond Recognition to Verify Chinese Text Rendering
abstract: A target-conditioned verifier using Ideographic Description Sequences detects local Chinese text rendering errors and improves generation through reinforcement learning.

title: Acting Through Registers
abstract: RegisterWAM reorganizes visual representations via learnable registers and flow-matching supervision to suppress spatial outliers and improve robot action learning.

title: The COUNT: Counting N-grams Unlocks Scaling on Host Memory and Training-Free Adaptation
abstract: COUNT improves language model efficiency by using precomputed n-gram counts stored in host memory to augment embeddings without learned parameters, boosting performance and enabling domain adaptation at inference.

title: Continuum Attention
abstract: Continuum Attention replaces discrete key-value lookup with continuous integration over a piecewise linear memory curve, improving language modeling performance while preserving standard Transformer architecture.

title: Generative World Simulation with DAO and JING
abstract: A generative framework couples a persistent shared world state with continuous first-person audiovisual generation to enable sustained interactive experiences that evolve through user actions.

title: Latent Compaction with Test-Time Training
abstract: Latent Compaction uses test-time training to learn compact, document-specific key-value caches that preserve retrieval accuracy under aggressive compression without requiring downstream questions.

title: SWEeper-Bench: Can Agents Discover Bugs in Interactive Software?
abstract: SWEeper-Bench evaluates coding agents on finding and fixing interaction-dependent bugs in web applications through interactive testing and browser-based verification.

title: Diff Diffusion: Predicting Edit Paths with Diffusion Models for Efficient Code Editing
abstract: Diff Diffusion is a diffusion-based language model framework that predicts structured code edits to enable fast, accurate, low-latency modifications in AI-assisted development environments.

title: Exploring the Limits of Combinatorial Generalization in Embodied Manipulation
abstract: Hierarchical Subtask Execution and Pose Robust Task Initialization improve skill recombination in long-horizon robot manipulation by closing start-state gaps at subtask transitions.

title: Training LLMs for Multi-Agent Collaboration with Verifiable Information Rewards
abstract: CoSIR trains LLM agents to collaborate by rewarding information sharing and usage via surprisal reduction, improving multi-agent performance on unseen tasks.

title: VASPO: Self-Distillation with Privileged Value Estimation
abstract: Value-Augmented Self-Distillation Policy Optimization integrates a self-teacher and critic within PPO to improve reasoning by combining token-level advantages with bounded probability ratios, boosting accuracy on mathematical benchmarks.

title: Rethinking LLM-Guided Visual Question Answering: Does Deeper Knowledge Integration Really Help?
abstract: Shallow late fusion of LLM-generated reasoning guidance outperforms deep attention injection in knowledge-based VQA under limited data, highlighting that integration depth should align with the training regime.

title: SyncReward: Human-Aligned Synchronization Reward for Audio-Visual Generation
abstract: Researchers introduce a dataset, benchmark, and reward model to evaluate and improve synchronization between generated audio and visual content.

title: Physical Time as a Missing Dimension of Robot Policy Memory Dynamics
abstract: Temporal Flow Policy integrates measured time intervals into robot memory dynamics to improve action timing and retention of past events across physical time.

title: PreciseCoder: Faithful and Generalizable Debugging Beyond Unit-Test Rewards
abstract: PreciseCoder improves code repair by rewarding precise, localized edits rather than only unit-test passage, reducing unnecessary changes and improving generalization across model sizes.

title: Choosing LLMs for Strategic Agent Interactions
abstract: Strategic model selection for game-theoretic LLM evaluation reveals that multi-armed bandit methods outperform embedding-based selectors but remain below fixed-model baselines against adaptive opponents.

title: To Align or Not To Align: Check Your COMPASS Before You Train
abstract: COMPASS estimates model-pair compatibility before alignment or merging by measuring local neighborhood overlap and paradigm limits, guiding resource allocation across cross-modal and merging tasks.

title: Vela: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models with Adaptive Action Curve Parametrization
abstract: Vela is a vision-language-action model that uses continuous spline-based trajectories to adapt temporal resolution for robot manipulation, improving long-horizon planning and local precision.

title: Jag: Direct Box Prediction for Efficient Visual Grounding
abstract: Jag adapts a compact pretrained multimodal model to predict bounding boxes directly via a regression head, improving grounding accuracy and reducing inference latency.

title: NavGPT-3: Harnessing Context in a Hierarchical Navigation Runtime
abstract: NavGPT-3 integrates long-horizon reasoning with low-latency action policies via an OS-like runtime, achieving human-level embodied navigation performance.

title: MimicX: Policy-in-the-Loop Supervision Refinement for Video-Driven Humanoid Motion Tracking
abstract: MimicX improves humanoid motion tracking by using execution feedback to refine video-driven policies, reducing tracking errors and extending robust execution horizons.

title: G^3VLA: Geometric Inductive Bias for Vision-Language-Action Models
abstract: G³VLA injects calibrated multi-camera geometry into vision-language-action models via ray embeddings and cross-view fusion, improving robot manipulation without changing the action space.

title: MA-Bench: Measuring Operational Planning in Language Models
abstract: MA-Bench evaluates language models on synthesizing contradictory military planning documents into structured briefs, finding that even top models achieve only 62% of expert rubric requirements with inference and omission errors being common.

title: Your Transformer Is Secretly Elastic
abstract: The method converts pre-trained transformers into elastic models that adapt continuously to varying computational budgets by jointly ranking and softly pruning individual neurons and attention heads across multiple sparsity targets without retraining.

title: StreamErase: Towards Ultra-Fast Streaming Video Erasing
abstract: StreamErase enables real-time, streaming video object removal with sub-second latency by transferring erasing capabilities from a bidirectional model to an efficient unidirectional streaming generator using sliding-window causal attention with attention sinks.

title: AgentSafeEvo: Adversarial Co-Evolution for LLM Agent Safety
abstract: AgentSafeEvo uses adversarial co-evolution to train LLM agents to resist malicious tool-use attacks across diverse tasks without sacrificing general capabilities.

title: When Left Is Right? Camera-Motion Understanding beyond Screen
abstract: CameraVLM improves vision-language model understanding of camera motion by jointly learning off-screen motion states and on-screen flow dynamics with language-aligned training.

title: History Replays Itself: Unleashing Long-Context Capability in Linear Attention
abstract: NoteBank augments linear attention models with a sparse episodic memory that stores selected text and replays it through native computation, greatly improving long-context retrieval without extra training or significant overhead.

title: Self-Conditioning Enables Deep Sequential Reasoning in Flow Matching
abstract: Flow matching with self-conditioning enables deeper visual reasoning by allowing iterative sampling steps to increase expressive power beyond constant-depth limits.

title: Next-Concept Modeling: Fast, Parallel Coarse-to-Fine Text Generation
abstract: Next-Concept Modeling uses hierarchical discrete codes and parallel level-wise generation to accelerate diffusion language models while improving quality and reasoning performance.

title: VLX-Go: Robust Embodied Tracking through Multi-Stage Learning and On-Policy Refinement
abstract: A vision-language waypoint policy using staged multimodal training improves robot tracking of intended people among distractors and benefits from on-policy refinement.

title: Lluna: Collaborative Unimodal Models for Missing-Modality Inference
abstract: Lluna improves multimodal predictions under missing inputs by combining private unimodal predictions with graph-based residual collaboration and progressive consistency training.

title: Looking Complete Is Not Being Grounded: Evaluating LLM Sitreps Against Human-Authored Situation Reports
abstract: LLM-generated crisis reports match human performance on some metrics but fail to supply professional provenance and reproduce few official figures, while common automatic scores poorly reflect completeness.

title: Drive3R: Block-wise Streaming Geometric Foundation Models for Autonomous Driving
abstract: Drive3R is a block-wise streaming geometric foundation model that enables scalable, long-horizon multi-view 3D reconstruction for autonomous driving by using block-wise causal attention and confidence-aware re-anchoring to reduce drift and maintain global consistency.

title: Cortex: Measurement-Gated Evolution and Pruning of Coding-Agent Skills and Rules
abstract: Cortex validates agent harness updates by replaying developer corrections, retaining only rules and skills that consistently improve performance without degrading tasks.

title: The Agent Knew: Internal States Forecast Unauthorized Actions and Stop Them, and the Lies That Follow
abstract: Residual-stream forecasting detects unauthorized agent actions and false reports before they occur, enabling low-cost gating that reduces violations and prompt-injection attacks without harming task completion.

title: A Diagnostic Study of World-Space Human Recovery Under High Camera Dynamics
abstract: A scale mismatch between independently recovered camera and human estimates causes severe world-space drift in fast-motion dance videos, which is corrected by a closed-form rescaling method that stabilizes multi-person reconstruction without retraining.

title: Can Learning to Answer Spatial Questions Improve Novel-View Generation?
abstract: Generating novel views from limited observations requires preserving both the appearance and spatial structure of a scene. Although recent approaches exploit fine-grained geometric cues, they do not explicitly model high-level semantic and spatial properties such as object identity, attributes, and inter-object relationships. In this work, we investigate whether 3D language understanding can provide complementary supervision for novel-view generation. We introduce Ask4NV, built on a pretrained unified multimodal model with a Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) architecture. Our model incorporates camera geometry into both VAE and ViT representations and leverages understanding features during generation through joint self-attention with a modality-aware attention masking strategy. Experiments demonstrate strong image quality and geometric consistency in novel-view generation, alongside competitive 3D language understanding. Further analysis shows that joint training improves cross-view correspondence in VAE representations and similarity in a 3D-aware feature space.

title: Modeling and Understanding Neural Weights of Humanoid Policies with Diffusion
abstract: Recent advances in robot learning have driven rapid progress in humanoid control, enabling increasingly agile behaviors in the real world. However, humanoid control networks are typically obtained through conventional training procedures, while comparatively little attention has been given to directly modeling the distribution of their learned weights and generating functional networks in weight space. In this work, we investigate whether high-performing humanoid control networks can be generatively modeled directly through their weights. We adopt a latent diffusion framework that couples a linear autoencoder with a Diffusion Transformer. The autoencoder compresses actor network parameters into a compact latent space, and the Diffusion Transformer models the distribution of these latents. Trained on networks collected from reinforcement learning for the Unitree G1 robot, our approach generates deployable networks that perform various motions in the real world, including walking, dancing, and spin kick. Beyond generation, we further study the learned weight space to better understand the structure captured by these humanoid control networks. We identify a structural principle in the first-layer weights that consistently reflects the robot's kinematic prior. Notably, this kinematic prior emerges under both Reinforcement Learning (RL) and Imitation Learning (IL) training, suggesting that it is not specific to a particular optimization process but may instead reflect common knowledge associated with humanoid embodiment. Together, these results demonstrate the feasibility of generative modeling in humanoid network weight space, while providing initial insights into the information encoded by their learned weights. Additional results are available on our project website: https://humanoid-weight-diffusion.github.io/

title: Representation Conditioning for Generation
abstract: Representation-alignment methods effectively accelerate the diffusion transformer training. REPA, for example, uses a pretrained vision encoder to supervise an intermediate layer through an MLP projection head which is discarded after training. It aims to import semantics from the vision encoder to the diffusion backbone. While this objective is achieved at early layers by back-propagating the alignment loss, there is no guarantee that later layers, supervised by the velocity prediction loss alone, can well access such semantics. We propose a simple solution, representation conditioning (RECON), to improve semantics in later layers. During training, we feed the pretrained vision encoder tokens into later layers; during inference, because we no longer have the clean image, we reuse the MLP head (as a proxy to the vision encoder) and project its output tokens to the later layers. Our method adds no parameters and leads to much faster convergence: RECON is $63\times$ faster than SiT and $25\times$ faster than REPA. Code is available at https://github.com/saeidrazavi/RECON

title: Hierarchical Residual Policy Learning for Real-World Mobile Manipulation with Sparse Human Guidance
abstract: Mobile Manipulation (MoMa) is a cornerstone of autonomous robotic systems, yet real-world fine-tuning remains a formidable challenge because of high-dimensional action spaces and intricate coupling between heterogeneous modules. In this paper, we propose HiRe-MoMa (Hierarchical Residual Mobile Manipulation), a systematic framework for stable and sample-efficient real-world fine-tuning of complex MoMa systems. At its core, HiRe-MoMa adopts a Hierarchical Residual Architecture that fine-tunes a frozen base policy. A Policy-Agnostic Residual learns additive corrections atop the base policy, while Hierarchical Decoupling splits the residual into mobile-base and manipulator-arm heads with unidirectional conditioning, mitigating gradient interference and aligning corrections with the platform's physical hierarchy. To improve sample efficiency in data-expensive real-world settings, we propose Expert-Guided Value Alignment, which leverages sparse human interventions with under 20% training coverage to reshape the critic's value landscape, effectively guiding autonomous exploration through expert priors. Extensive real-world experiments on the TIAGo++ platform demonstrate that HiRe-MoMa consistently enhances task performance with only around 30 minutes of online interaction, regardless of the base policy architecture. To our knowledge, this is among the first frameworks to enable efficient on-robot fine-tuning for mobile manipulation in the real world, providing a practical paradigm for deploying complex robotic systems in dynamic, human-centric environments. Further details can be found on our project website: https://hire-moma.github.io/

title: CommerceGen-Studio: An End-to-End Framework for Commercial-Grade Main-Image Generation
abstract: We present CommerceGen-Studio, an end-to-end framework for generating commercial-grade main images for e-commerce Stock Keeping Units (SKUs). Our framework is organized along a three-stage pipeline of information extraction, semantic rewriting, and multi-condition generation: Prompt-Eval-Refine-Loop Agent (PERL-Agent) distills heterogeneous SKU metadata into concise selling-point text lists through an iterative closed loop of VLM and LLM roles scored by a reference-free rubric. Layout Thinker Optimization (LTO) aligns the rewriter with both caption and rendered-image quality via alternating domain-specific policy optimization. SKU-DiT, trained under Reinforce-Distill-Reinforce (RDR) progressive training, conditions jointly on the white-background product image, the trademark crop, and the structured layout to hold subject fidelity, trademark integrity, and character-level text accuracy together. The framework runs in production at a scale of millions of main images per day with a latency of a few seconds per image, which we believe makes it among the first systems of this kind to operate at commercial scale. We also release CommerceGen-Bench, a benchmark of hard cases collected from live traffic across all product categories. On it, our framework achieves the highest overall scores among the evaluated open-source baselines on both editing tracks, with and without prompt enhancement. It also matches much larger closed-source models, and beats several of them at Instruction Following and Product Integration - the two properties that determine whether an image can be published.

title: DynThinker: Unifying Static 3D and Dynamic 4D Spatial Reasoning
abstract: Achieving general spatial intelligence requires a unified understanding of both static 3D and dynamic 4D. However, we find that existing models struggle to excel at both: 3D post-training can weaken dynamic understanding, while 4D-specialized models often lack strong static 3D reasoning. Our analysis reveals that this spatial--dynamic interference is highly non-uniform across parameter groups, with the balance between static and dynamic capabilities particularly sensitive to changes in late-layer MLPs. To address this interference, we propose DynThinker, a unified framework for jointly strengthening static and dynamic spatial reasoning. Decoupled Exponential Moving Average (D-EMA) applies configurable group-wise averaging to constrain drift in interference-sensitive pretrained parameters while preserving flexibility for capability enhancement. Spatial-Dynamic Fusion (SDF) complements D-EMA by selectively integrating spatial and temporal priors from a dynamic geometry encoder into intermediate VLM representations under semantic guidance. Across ten metrics spanning nine static 3D and dynamic 4D benchmarks, DynThinker achieves the highest average score among all evaluated models. Notably, DynThinker achieves 56.0 on ReVSI, 67.2 on DSR-Bench, and 51.2 and 40.1 under the sample-wise and group-wise evaluation protocols of DSI-Bench, respectively, setting new state-of-the-art results among the compared open-source models across all four evaluations within a unified model.

title: Co-Evolving Acting and Forecasting for Language Agents
abstract:
Training language agents is bottlenecked by the high cost of long-horizon rollouts, yet standard agentic reinforcement learning (RL) learns only from a terminal scalar reward, leaving the supervision in intermediate steps largely unused. Prior work exploits this supervision through value targets that estimate per-step success probabilities or observation targets that fit environment response. Both are hard to construct well: (1) value targets come from the same single scalar signal for each step in the trajectory, and (2) observation targets, such as web pages and terminal logs, are long and noisy and reach only one step ahead. We propose 
ame, which adds a third kind of multi-step action targets. On successful on-policy trajectories, 
ame trains the policy backbone to generate the action sequences that follows each history. Each action is also supervised when forecast from the preceding histories, forming a temporal ensemble that the shared backbone absorbs during training, and this enables acting and forecasting to co-evolve. The policy still acts one step at a time at inference, with no overhead. Across five benchmarks (ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, WebShop, $τ^2$-bench, and AppWorld), 
ame (1) achieves stronger aggregate performance than GRPO and RL baselines with predictive auxiliary targets across simulated environments, while improving overall performance on both realistic applications; (2) delivers up to $1.9	imes$ and $2.0	imes$ higher sample efficiency than ECHO and GRPO, respectively, on ScienceWorld; and (3) achieves these gains with a single policy backbone, without additional models, separate pretraining, or inference overhead. The codebase is available at https://github.com/ulab-uiuc/CoPE.

title: GeoThinker-$F$: Endogenous Predictive World Representations for Fast Spatial Intelligence
abstract: Existing geometry-aware Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) increasingly rely on external 3D encoders to provide structural priors, but executing these additional encoder paths at inference introduces substantial latency and computational overhead. We propose GeoThinker-$F$, an efficient framework that internalizes spatiotemporal perception by transforming causal MLLM hidden states into predictive latent world representations. Our key insight is that intermediate semantic representations contain sufficient information to predict useful representations of current geometry and future semantics, without requiring an exact reproduction of features from a dedicated 3D encoder. To realize this idea, GeoThinker-$F$ adopts a decoupled two-stage training strategy. In the first stage, the MLLM backbone is frozen while lightweight Latent Frame Prediction (LFP) heads learn from an offline 3D geometry expert and next-frame semantic targets. In the second stage, the external expert is removed, and the model is jointly optimized to generate and selectively integrate its self-predicted priors through a specialized Spatial-Grounded Temporal (SGT) Fusion module. Extensive evaluations show that GeoThinker-$F$ eliminates runtime dependence on external 3D geometry encoders while maintaining competitive performance across diverse spatial intelligence benchmarks. It achieves up to a $3.6\times$ inference speedup, reducing latency from $1.45\,\mathrm{s}$ to $0.40\,\mathrm{s}$ while retaining strong spatial reasoning performance.

title: Feed-Forward Multi-View Feature Coding for 3D Gaussian Splatting
abstract: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) methods enable efficient reconstruction of 3D scenes from sparse multi-view images in a single forward pass, without scene-specific optimization. However, existing feed-forward scene-coding pipelines first generate a complete Gaussian representation and then encode its geometry and appearance attributes separately, often involving non-differentiable operations. The resulting 'generate-then-compress' pipeline requires complex attribute-specific codec designs and limits rate-distortion performance by restricting the exploitation of cross-attribute redundancy. We propose multi-view feature coding for Gaussian splatting (MFGS), an end-to-end feed-forward framework for scene coding. Instead of compressing an explicit Gaussian representation, MFGS extracts multi-view features from the input images and encodes them into a compact bitstream. Through end-to-end rate-distortion training, MFGS learns compact multi-view features that jointly represent geometry and appearance, enabling the receiver to predict Gaussian attributes from the decoded features. We further introduce importance-guided Gaussian selection to accommodate different rendering budgets, allowing the receiver to adjust the number of Gaussians used for rendering from the same bitstream. Across RE10K, ACID, and DL3DV, MFGS achieves 99.76-99.86% bitrate savings over the generate-then-compress pipeline, as measured by BD-rate, while reducing total GMACs by 52-55% and providing an approximately 12 times end-to-end speedup.

title: Price of Anarchy of First-Price Auctions in Agentic Markets
abstract: An agentic market is a decentralized serving-time market where AI agents bid to claim each user prompt. An agent's bid is based on its expected value for the prompt, which is the expectation of the reward for its response minus its inference costs. First-price auctions (FPAs), in which the highest bidder pays its bid and receives the prompt, are a natural way to allocate prompts in such a market, since they are simple and transparent to run, and do not require central knowledge of private capabilities and costs. However, FPAs are not truthful: participants may bid less than their true value in the hope of a larger profit, and the prompt may then be allocated to someone other than the bidder who values it the most. This welfare loss is quantified by the $\textit{price-of-anarchy}$ (PoA). In this paper, we argue that agentic markets are likely to possess features that reduce the price-of-anarchy. The first is a $\textit{competitive floor}$, which occurs when multiple bidders usually value the prompt above some baseline share of the optimal welfare (e.g., because the best models are often distilled into cheaper alternatives, which perform similarly). We show that competition among them then limits the welfare loss, which can be driven to zero as the floor rises. The second feature is $\textit{near-independence}$ of values after conditioning on the prompt, which occurs when most of the predictable variation in the expected value is determined by the difficulty of the prompt. As the value distribution approaches conditional independence, we can derive an efficiency guarantee that approaches a factor of $1 - 1/e^2$ of the optimal welfare. Thus, both features give rise to welfare lower bounds that are significantly better than the well-known general case of $1 - 1/e$. We validate these results empirically using auctions with strategic bidders simulated on the EmbedLLM prompt routing dataset.

title: Learnable Hodge-Laplacian Driven Mixture of Experts for Steady-PDE Surrogates on Coarse Unstructured Meshes
abstract: Current approaches for steady partial differential equations surrogate models on unstructured meshes apply a single mixing mechanism to the whole solution. This paper proposes an architecture that partitions the solution among vanilla transformer experts, each focused on a different spectral scale. The partition is built from a discrete Hodge Laplacian $L_0=\star_0^{-1} d_0^{\top}\star_1 d_0$, that serves as a fitting layer measuring high-frequency content. A gating mechanism takes the mesh as input and produces the per-vertex weights that recombine the expert outputs. AirFRANS is a steady Reynolds-averaged Navier--Stokes (RANS) airfoil benchmark. We evaluate our approach in a reduced remeshed version of the benchmark with each unstructured mesh counting 9.6K faces and 4.9K vertices. We compare our approach with the Transolver on the same dataset and dataset slit. Our approach reduces relative $L_2$ error by 31\% and interior mean squared error by 47\%.

title: One Task, Many Interfaces: Simple Cross-Interface Consistency Training Improves LLM Agent Robustness
abstract: Post-training binds the competence of an LLM agent to the interface it was trained on. Semantics-preserving perturbations of that interface, such as renaming an action or changing the notation, leave the underlying task unchanged yet make the agent worse at it. Scoring each sample independently means interface randomization only broadens this dependence from a single interface to the training interface distribution, so out-of-distribution perturbations still degrade the agent. We propose Cross-Interface Policy Regularization (CIPR), a self-supervised objective that replaces action names with uninformative identifiers and presents each training sample under two interfaces in which equivalent actions are identified by construction. CIPR penalizes the KL divergence between the action distributions induced under the two interfaces, so the policy behaves consistently across them. We evaluate CIPR in both supervised and reinforcement-learning post-training, where it improves robustness. On agentic function calling, held-out interface perturbations reduce the accuracy of a post-trained agent by nearly 25%, and CIPR recovers 10.5% while leaving accuracy on the unchanged interface intact.

title: Beyond LLM Judge: Mechanical Verification for Agentic Autoformalization
abstract: We introduce a novel method for verifying Lean formalizations that goes beyond LLM-judged faithfulness. Unlike most verification methods, which rely on LLMs or trained models, our method combines LLM-based semantic review with mechanical numerical and vacuity checks, providing checkable feedback and detecting errors missed by LLM judges. We apply this method, along with our Extract-Verify-Proof autoformalization pipeline, to construct the Formalized Library of Mathematical Functions (FLMF), a partial formalization of the NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions (DLMF). On three labeled datasets, our method achieves the lowest accepted-error rate among the evaluated methods, measured as the fraction of incorrect statements accepted by the verification method. Expert review of the results also identifies translation and source defects in existing datasets. Code available at https://github.com/annamei1/FLMF-Ch7ErrFunc-Release.git.

title: Manacá-1B-Instruct-2: Reproducible Safety Alignment for a Native Brazilian-Portuguese LLM. Negative DPO Results, a Controlled Composition Scan, and a Silent Failure Mode of the LLM Judge
abstract: Brazilian Portuguese remains underserved by open-source language models, and the few that are safety-aligned rarely document what did not work or validate comparisons with statistical significance. We present Manacá-1B-Instruct-2, the second-generation post-training alignment of Manacá-1B (1.72B parameters, trained from scratch for PT-BR), with an SFT corpus of 291,223 examples. We document three DPO attempts, all negative, including a case where the training reward margin reaches 1.0 while free generation does not change at all, and show that safety came from a dedicated safety-SFT (LLM-jp AnswerCarefully style), refined over three iterations until closing the safety-helpfulness frontier. A controlled scan of the fraction of general data in the safety-SFT mix (10% to 60%) reveals a non-monotonic over-refusal curve with a knee point at 40-50%. The final model is compared against four external PT-BR models on the same items, with Wilson confidence intervals and paired McNemar tests with Holm-Bonferroni correction: the lower bound of its safety interval (94.1%) lies above the upper bound of all four baselines. We also report a methodological finding for LLM-judge evaluation: on two of six safety items in MT-Bench-PT, the judge categorically refuses to assign a score regardless of the evaluated response, silently reducing the effective N of that category in every prior report of the project. We complement this with an n-gram decontamination check and a Chinchilla-anchored compute-budget table that attributes the gap in general capability to pre-training scale rather than alignment methodology. All code, raw data, logs, and scripts that produce every reported number are publicly released.

title: Scaling Discovery Requires Forgetting
abstract:
Automated research with LLM agents has shown promising results in various domains. Through iterative refinement and scored verifiers, LLM agents are capable of discovering new ideas. There are different ways to scale automated research: let one agent iterate for longer, run several agents in parallel, or further let the parallel agents communicate and build on one another's candidates. However, we find that all three strategies eventually plateau as the agents accumulate history. Each agent becomes anchored to its own past attempts, making fewer and smaller edits. Beyond this point, additional budget brings little further improvement. In this paper, we show that the key to scaling discovery further is to forget. Periodically discarding the search state, including every agent's session and the candidate history, and restarting from the best candidate found so far, unblocks the search and pushes the same budget further.
  We implement forgetting in a team of agents with communication and evaluate it on four tasks spanning heuristic programming, kernel optimization and model training. The results show up to 15% improvement compared to parallel agents, and up to 39% compared to a single agent. Our results suggest that, for open-ended discovery, what an agent is allowed to remember matters as much as how much compute it is given.

title: A$^3$PreCore: Robust Rigid Registration for Native FLAIR-Space Brain-Mask Transfer
abstract: Reliable brain-mask transfer into native fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) space can fail when T1-to-FLAIR rigid registration is unstable. We developed A$^3$PreCore, a six-degree-of-freedom rigid-registration strategy that aligns the full bias-corrected T1-weighted image to native FLAIR using normalized mutual information while preserving the established T1-space anatomical mask. We also introduced extended quantitative quality control (E-QC), which characterizes mask extent, field-of-view-relative position, FLAIR intensity support, boundary support, inferior morphology, and pairwise geometric disagreement. In 78 participants with paired T1-weighted and FLAIR imaging, A$^3$PreCore was compared with fsl_anat and the Brain Extraction Tool (BET). Gross rigid-body misregistration occurred in 21/78 fsl_anat outputs (26.9%) and 0/78 A$^3$PreCore outputs (exact two-sided McNemar p=9.54 x 10^-7). Among 57 participants without gross fsl_anat misregistration, A$^3$PreCore preserved close agreement (median Dice=0.993; median paired Delta NMI=-0.00007, p=0.429). A$^3$PreCore remained broadly concordant with BET (median Dice=0.955), with less inferior and extracranial extension in representative comparisons. Method-blinded neuroscientists ranked A$^3$PreCore first in 35/40 participants (87.5%). E-QC additionally exposed severe orientation-related disagreement not evident from global descriptors or centroid displacement alone. These findings support A$^3$PreCore as a robust native-FLAIR brain-mask transfer strategy and E-QC as a complementary framework for multidimensional mask characterization and participant-specific geometric quality control.

title: PhySGA: A Physics-Space Grounded Agentic Framework for Generalizable and Interactive 3D Composition
abstract: 3D object composition is pivotal to digital content creation and robot simulation, while also serving as a critical testbed for physical intelligence in foundation models. Previous methods either leverage large language models to directly predict object coordinates, or utilize generative diffusion priors to synthesize composite images for visual alignment, both of which rely on static priors in digital spaces. However, these methods consistently struggle with complex compositions such as precise hanging, gravity-driven settling and hidden containment, as these tasks require interactive construction processes involving global planning, fine-grained alignment, and physical simulation. To address these challenges, we propose PhySGA, a Physics-Space Grounded Agentic Framework for 3D composition via agent exploration and physical simulation, enabling the universal interactive assembly of rigid, articulated, and deformable objects. Directly applying vanilla LLMs or VLMs to this task proves insufficient, as current models inherently lack grounded physical understanding and interactive construction experience. To overcome this limitation, we design a collaborative feedforward-feedback architecture: an Assembly Agent focuses on geometric and kinematic reasoning for global step planning and coarse adjustment, while a Critic Agent reasons over contact dynamics for simulator state diagnosis and fine-grained closed-loop correction. Furthermore, Action Routers map semantic planning and analysis onto executable physical primitives within the simulator, while a task-specific Self-Evolving Skill Library distills historical trial-and-error feedback into reusable experiences, boosting success rates and minimizing exploration attempts. Extensive experiments within Isaac Sim demonstrate that PhySGA significantly surpasses existing methods in relation fidelity, physical plausibility, and visual quality.

title: Speculative Sampling in Interactive Video Generation
abstract: Interactive video generation commonly relies on small bidirectional chunks to reduce response latency. Yet our preliminary experiments show that larger chunks improve video quality and better utilize GPU parallelism, allowing more latents to be sampled with only a modest increase in sampling time. Motivated by these observations, we propose Speculative Sampling, a strategy that combines the modeling power of large bidirectional windows with the low-latency interaction of small ones. It expands the modeling window by appending noise latents as padding and caches the resulting predictions for reuse when the condition remains unchanged. Predictions are delivered incrementally, while the uncommitted future remains replaceable. Our latency analysis shows that this removes the waiting-time lower bound imposed by chunk boundaries, shifting the optimization focus from reducing chunk size to accelerating per-chunk sampling. Bidirectional window size thus becomes a decision variable for jointly optimizing visual quality and sampling time, rather than a necessary constraint on low-latency interaction. This opens a path to serving large bidirectional models in interactive streaming systems without complex streaming post-training.

title: PerSo: Investigating Facets of LLMs' Social Intelligence in Real-World Persuasion Scenarios
abstract: Understanding the social intelligence of large language models (LLMs) is increasingly important for applications involving human-AI interaction and multi-agent environments. Social intelligence comprises two aspects: cognitive intelligence, the ability to infer others' mental states, and behavioral intelligence, the ability to select appropriate social actions based on these inferences to achieve social goals. Persuasion provides a natural testbed in which both aspects are simultaneously at play, yet prior benchmarks typically evaluate them in isolation using synthetic scenarios. We introduce PerSo, a benchmark that evaluates both aspects on real-world persuasion dialogues from Reddit's ChangeMyView community, using an LLM-in-the-loop pipeline to construct the evaluation tasks, validated through human annotation. Our evaluation of diverse LLMs shows that performance generally scales with model size but varies across dimensions. The strongest LLM slightly surpasses the best observed human performance on the behavioral task, while the best human participant remains ahead on the cognitive task.

title: Detection of Potato Plant Leaf Diseases using Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: Potato is an important food-security crop in Ethiopia, but its production is affected by foliar diseases, particularly early blight and late blight. This study develops a lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) to classify potato leaves into three categories: healthy, early blight, and late blight. The proposed model was trained using 2,215 images from the PlantVillage dataset and evaluated on an independent field dataset containing 247 images collected from potato farms in Banja, Awi Zone, Ethiopia. On PlantVillage, the model achieved 99.04% training accuracy, 98.21% validation accuracy, and 98.66% test accuracy. On the field dataset, it achieved 90.28% accuracy. The study also compares the proposed CNN with VGG16 and MobileNetV2 in terms of classification performance and computational efficiency. The proposed model contains 446,787 trainable parameters, occupies approximately 1.70 MB, and requires an average of 5.58 seconds per training epoch in the reported experimental setup, compared with 9.96 seconds for VGG16 and 7.68 seconds for MobileNetV2. The results demonstrate the potential of a compact CNN for potato leaf disease classification and highlight the importance of independent field evaluation, where image conditions are more variable than in controlled benchmark datasets. The proposed approach may support preliminary disease identification for smallholder farmers in Ethiopia and similar agricultural settings.

title: Reliability-Aware Multimodal Sentiment Prediction Under Local Modality Missingness
abstract: Multimodal sentiment models are usually evaluated on complete utterances, yet streams often lose a contiguous span of text, audio, or video. We study local missingness on aligned CMU-MOSEI features. Our reliability-aware network (RM-Net) keeps the original temporal positions, represents unobserved positions with a learned token, outputs bounded per-modality intensity contributions gated by observation quality, and is trained with dual-view masking of contiguous segments. We fuse five RM-Net seeds with a LoRA-adapted BERT text expert, using a fusion weight that depends only on the visible fraction of content tokens. Architecture, checkpoint, and fusion choices were made on the validation split. On the held-out split, the fused model reaches a macro-F1 of 0.655 on clean inputs and 0.634 under 40\% mixed missingness; its two-view average exceeds the auxiliary-head baseline by 0.024 (95\% video-cluster bootstrap interval [0.003, 0.045]). Because this split was inspected during development, these numbers are not a blind test. For explanations, exact Shapley attributions over the eight modality subsets and position-level occlusion show that top-ranked positions reduce the predicted-class probability faster than random positions (AUC gap 0.113 on validation). We also describe an auditable word-level alignment pipeline for raw clips; its outputs do not feed the predictive models.

title: PrismaCoder: Pushing the Boundaries of Open Multimodal Code Intelligence through Decomposed Rubric Synthesis
abstract: Multimodal code intelligence connects the symbolic world of programs with the visual world their execution creates. Interest in this capability is burgeoning, as models are increasingly asked to produce charts, webpages, animations, and semi-structured documents. Recently, proprietary models have pushed far ahead, producing interactive artifacts even from a text description or a screenshot alone. Yet their data and training remain closed, and open progress is held back by the quantity and quality of available data and by the pipelines and methods for producing it. Quality is the harder of the two, since a sample must be correct as a program, well built, and above all visually right once rendered. No existing signal covers all three. Execution often returns just a pass or fail, code similarity does not map to the visual output, and task-specific verifiers do not generalize. To push open progress further, we start from the data side with PrismaForge, a hierarchical data pipeline centered on a synthesized rubric that decomposes these factors into checkable criteria. The same rubric serves as both filter and reward: it curates the supervised corpus, then drives reinforcement learning on visual-coding tasks. Leveraging PrismaForge for data synthesis and filtering, we build PrismaCoder-2M, the most diverse open dataset for multimodal code intelligence and the largest to date. On the model side, we train PrismaCoder-9B and PrismaCoder-35B on this data and release both. They lead the open state of the art by a wide margin and rival leading proprietary systems. Our analyses further show that the proposed rubric-based pipeline improves multimodal coding performance across model backbones. We release our code and data at https://qiushisun.github.io/PrismaCoder-Home/.

title: Revisiting Simple Baselines for Relational Deep Learning
abstract: Relational deep learning has emerged as a powerful paradigm for learning end-to-end predictive models over relational databases by representing them as temporal heterogeneous graphs. Recent advances based on graph neural networks and Transformers have achieved strong performance across diverse domains. However, the effectiveness of simpler relational baselines remains underexplored, making it difficult to assess how much architectural complexity is needed to achieve strong predictive performance. Motivated by the observation that predictive signals arise from target attributes, relational attributes, and historical labels, we revisit how effectively these signals can be exploited using simple propagation methods. We adapt fixed low-pass feature propagation to relational entity graphs and train an MLP for prediction. The resulting predictions are further refined using Correct-and-Smooth, a graph-based label propagation algorithm that incorporates historical labels over task-specific meta-graphs connecting target entities. Across classification and regression tasks on RelBench, an MLP trained on neighborhood-filtered features outperforms one using only target-entity features on most tasks and recovers a substantial portion of the performance of heterogeneous GNNs. Correct-and-Smooth provides further gains from historical labels, although applying it requires a separately constructed meta-graph because connections among target entities are not directly specified by the relational entity graph. Together, our studies revisit the effectiveness of established propagation methods as simple RDL baselines while identifying canonical meta-graph construction as a key challenge for effective label propagation.

title: Generative Representation Learning for Scalable Latent Tokenization
abstract: We introduce an approach for self-supervised representation learning designed to be used as a tokenizer for generative modeling. Our objective supervises a representation loss by factorizing the pointwise mutual information of the data, which we estimate by taking information differences between conditional predictions from a learned generative model. We justify our algorithm theoretically and empirically, demonstrating that our generative approach to representation learning avoids dimensional collapse and feature suppression in cases where commonly used methods like DINO and LeJEPA fail. Moreover, we show our representation learning technique is scalable; expending more compute leads to predictably better latent tokenization. For the first time, we perform a careful analysis of the combined flop efficiency of tokenizer and generative model and demonstrate that our approach is a compute-optimal improvement over direct diffusion for pixel-space generation, obtaining an FID-50K of 2.18 with JiT-L. Applied to ImageNet and the text-to-image dataset GPIC, we show tokenizer encoder scaling laws for diffusability, where extrapolating our approach achieves representations in 7x fewer FLOPs than DINOv2 on ImageNet and 8x fewer FLOPs than WebSSL on GPIC.

title: ActiveEvidence: Decision-Focused Evidence Graphs with Verifiable Acquisition Gaps
abstract: A multimodal agent must decide whether visual evidence is worth acquiring, which candidate or resolution to query, and when further interaction can no longer change its decision. We study this problem under a strict free-metadata/paid-observation boundary, stochastic vector costs, and a frozen execution trace, and treat it as decision-certifiable active evidence acquisition. A Counterfactual Evidence Interaction Graph (CEIG) represents unary evidence value, signed second-order interaction, and directed conditional harm while maintaining explicit score enclosures for unresolved interactions; a decision-weighted enclosure objective tightens the bounds that can change action identity. Gap-directed refinement evaluates only interactions that can displace the incumbent acquisition and stops once an $ε$-decision certificate shows that unresolved terms cannot change the selected action beyond a declared tolerance. The certificate is model-relative: it verifies policy-consistent optimality under the pinned learned score, and semantic quality is measured separately through post-freeze labels. Paired continuation rollouts learn the downstream value of paid previews, an online operational cost filter is separated from independent finite-policy-family trajectory certification, and an acquisition monitor with an independently implemented verifier binds every certificate to the frozen trace. On 640 cases split into 384/128/128 training, validation, and test cases, the controller reaches task score 0.842, grounding F1 0.816, evidence recall 0.873, 1.74 accepted calls, 286.5K visual tokens, and 742ms p95 latency. Dense replay of issued certificates shows 0.992 action agreement and a 0.988 certificate rate while evaluating 19.6 instead of 191.4 expensive interaction terms per decision.

title: The Physics Is the Network: Fast, Training-Free Neural Emulation
abstract: Neural emulation need not require learning a substitute for known physics. We investigate PolyNets that couple a continuous-time neural representation of polynomial dynamics with a simple recurrent network for discrete-time integration. When the governing coefficients are known, the resulting tensor graph requires no training and preserves the prescribed numerical scheme while enabling efficient hardware execution and parallel simulation. Using the one-dimensional Korteweg-de Vries equation, we compare PolyNet with CPU and GPU finite-difference Runge-Kutta solvers and three trained neural models: a state-map emulator, a physics-informed predictor, and a learned-tendency integrator. Analytical soliton solutions provide a reference for amplitude and phase errors across grid resolutions, 10^6 dispersively scaled time steps, ensembles of up to 10^4 trajectories, and varying initial amplitudes. PolyNet achieves accuracy comparable to the numerical solvers, including at amplitudes outside the learned models' training conditions. It combines this fidelity with high GPU throughput, approximately constant over the tested resolution range, and favorable ensemble scaling.

title: The Wealth of Agents: Scaling Agentic AI Across Developers
abstract: Today's agentic systems are typically designed, built, and deployed by single developers with full control over all participating agents. While this simplifies development, it limits the potential scale of agentic systems. We study multi-developer agentic systems (MDAs) which enable developers to collaboratively build agentic systems to push frontier capability beyond what any individual developer could achieve alone. We construct empirical and theoretical models of developers to compare MDAs with single-developer agentic systems (SDAs). On GAIA, a general assistant benchmark, a population of specialized developers whose individual agents do not exceed 35% accuracy reaches 70% when their agents are combined in an MDA. This MDA performs 12 percentage points above the median general-purpose SDA built with several times each specialist's development budget. Our theoretical models show how MDAs can incentivize specialization and encourage more efficient use of aggregated developer resources. Put together, our results make a preliminary case for MDAs as a new scaling axis by enabling developers with diverse capabilities and resources to advance agentic AI collaboratively.

title: Bayesian Learning to Select Fair Classifiers
abstract: Evaluations of classifiers (AI or human or agents) often assume a batch setting in which every agent produces labels on every example in a test set, which can be expensive or impractical in many contexts. This motivates online policies that adaptively select agents to query as examples arrive and update policies as outcomes are observed. We study the problem of selecting, in an online stream, the agent that best balances (i) predictive performance and (ii) subgroup fairness of a sensitive attribute, and that allows for delayed observations of true class labels. We formulate this as a Bayesian multi-armed bandit problem using Thompson Sampling, explicitly balancing accuracy and fairness. We conduct empirical evaluations on real-world datasets spanning problems involving tabular classifiers, large language models, and human labelers, demonstrating substantial reductions in regret relative to baselines. Our theoretical contributions include guarantees on the performance of the selected agent that incorporate both the accuracy and fairness aspects of the problem.

title: A Two-Level Clinical Novelty Prioritization Framework for Disease Trajectories Discovered from Longitudinal Electronic Health Records
abstract: Graph-based analysis of electronic health records (EHRs) yields disease-trajectory catalogs, but structural support does not establish semantic novelty. We present a two-level framework to prioritize 99,527 branching motifs previously discovered by an upstream patient-disjoint, train-only MIMIC-IV v3.1 pipeline and frozen after validation-based catalog selection. The framework separates path-level and node-to-endpoint semantic sparsity from reliability-adjusted clinical priority. Three deterministic textualizations per motif or node-target pair were embedded with BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 and calibrated against 166,972 pre-2023 PubMed references using mean top-20 cosine distance. Positive recombination occurred in 8.63% of motifs and had negligible effect on global ranking, whereas specificity and support/GNN reliability terms changed clinical-priority ordering. Robustness analyses across neighbor counts, templates, encoders, generic-label taxonomies, score settings, PrimeKG, and corrected density-based RND showed that broad ordering was more stable than hard top-k membership. A semantic-dose analysis did not support a monotonic relation between score and forecasting benefit after endpoint and token-count adjustment (1.96 days per SD; 95% CI, -0.75 to 4.68). In the frozen catalog-q90 high-semantic subgroup, branch-enhanced forecasting reduced conditional event-time MAE by 20.1 days (95% CI, 13.3-27.0) and sMAPE by 2.37 percentage points (95% CI, 1.81-2.93), while discrimination and endpoint-ranking differences were inconclusive. Corrected RND showed low tail agreement with the primary score (Spearman rho = 0.430; q90 Jaccard = 0.125) despite a similar aggregate timing association. These findings support representation-aware, uncertainty-aware literature-relative prioritization of discovered trajectories rather than causal discovery or clinician-adjudicated novelty.

title: VascuSR: Iterative Anatomy-Aware Diffusion for CT Super-Resolution
abstract: Generative super-resolution (SR) can recover sharp detail in computed tomography (CT) images from severely downsampled observations, but the missing high-frequency content is not uniquely determined by the low-resolution input. Consequently, visually plausible reconstructions may contain anatomically unsupported vascular detail, such as missing, spurious, or incorrectly connected vessels. To overcome this challenge, we introduce VascuSR, an iterative anatomy-aware diffusion framework that combines image reconstruction with explicit 3D vascular guidance. First, to provide richer anatomical guidance, we use an explicit 3D vascular representation that captures structural information beyond individual slices. This representation also simplifies vascular refinement by allowing a lightweight 3D generative refiner to focus on vascular structure rather than complex CT appearance. Second, to guide slice-wise SR, a lightweight anatomy controller injects the refined structure into the diffusion decoder, while iterative feedback updates this guidance from each new SR volume. On re-annotated MSD Task08 and HVM datasets, VascuSR outperforms interpolation and learning-based SR baselines in segmentation accuracy (Dice and clDice) and 3D vascular structure (connectivity and mean centerline distance), while maintaining image quality comparable to its SR backbone. Compared with learning-based baselines, VascuSR reduces class-averaged connected-component counts by over 20% on both datasets and mean centerline distance by over 10% on MSD.

title: ReaDy: Recurrent States as Dynamic Context for Speculative Drafting in Hybrid Linear Attention Large Language Models
abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates autoregressive generation by drafting multiple tokens per step, yet feature-based drafters rely on target hidden features whose contextual emphasis may not align with the needs of subsequent draft positions. Hybrid linear attention (HLA) models maintain compact recurrent states that accumulate historical associations, offering an efficient source of complementary context for speculative drafting. We introduce ReaDy, the first speculative decoding method, to the best of our knowledge, to leverage HLA recurrent states for position-specific context retrieval during drafting. ReaDy equips each draft position with a learned query to retrieve supplementary context directly from the target's committed recurrent states. A lightweight state reader integrates this context into draft representations through residual updates, while low-rank state reads and fused operators keep additional computation and I/O overhead low. Building on DSpark's parallel backbone and sequential prediction head, ReaDy employs a lightweight two-stage adaptation strategy, with reader capacity, state sources, and residual placement examined through ablation studies. Across seven benchmarks spanning mathematics, code generation, and dialogue, ReaDy achieves an average $3.16\times$ decoding speedup over autoregressive decoding with Qwen3.8-27B on a single NVIDIA B200 GPU. It outperforms DSpark on every benchmark, improving throughput by 7.97% and acceptance length by 8.50% on average. Our code is available at https://github.com/StartLuxLabs/ReaDy.

title: Graph-Enhanced Disease Trajectory Discovery and Temporal Endpoint Forecasting from Longitudinal Electronic Health Records
abstract: Longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs) can reveal disease-progression structure, while useful forecasting requires leakage-controlled discovery, censor-aware outcomes, and inspectable trajectory evidence. We developed a graph-enhanced framework in MIMIC-IV v3.1 that splits patients before graph construction, learns train-only consecutive-admission transitions, and freezes endpoint-specific branching-motif policies selected on validation data. The final catalog contained 99,527 motifs, and a time-aware Transformer retrieved at most 24 patient-compatible motifs per endpoint through endpoint-specific cross-attention. Across five training seeds, micro-AUPRC increased from 0.9330 to 0.9357, while event-time MAE decreased from 676.9 to 657.7 days (reduction 19.2 days; 95% paired patient-cluster bootstrap CI, 13.8-24.8). Timing effects were heterogeneous: MAE worsened for events within 730 days but improved by 58.9 days for events occurring after 730 days. In an exploratory internal temporal split, branch conditioning reduced conditional event-time MAE by 26.9 days (95% CI, 23.0-30.8) without evidence of better micro-AUPRC. Corrected survival evaluation over the supported 0-2,555-day interval did not establish macro C-index or integrated Brier score superiority over a matched history-only discrete-hazard model. A directed, degree-matched GNN repair substantially improved unseen-edge discovery, yet replacing GNN-derived scores within fixed motif identities did not improve downstream forecasting. These results position branching motifs as structured trajectory context whose main value is long-range timing support rather than uniformly stronger endpoint discrimination, survival prediction, or causal explanation.

title: OLiVES: An Outdoor Low-Light Video Benchmark for Enhancement and Segmentation
abstract: Low-light video processing remains an underexplored problem in computer vision, primarily due to the scarcity of high-quality ground-truth data. Existing public datasets exhibit several limitations, including restricted motion diversity, limited scene coverage, weak degradations, reliance on auxiliary modalities such as event data, and misalignment between low-light inputs and ground truth. Furthermore, current datasets typically address either low-light enhancement or scene understanding, whereas these tasks should be considered jointly. We introduce \textbf{OLiVES}, a benchmark dataset for outdoor low-light videos with dynamic scenes, designed to support both low-light video enhancement (LLVE) and video object segmentation (VOS). The dataset addresses key content gaps by incorporating a diverse range of natural textures, animals, occlusions, dynamic activities, and close-up scenes. To the best of our knowledge, OLiVES is the first outdoor low-light video dataset captured using professional cinema-grade cameras. It provides over 25,000 aligned normal- and low-light frame pairs, along with over 46,000 VOS annotations. We benchmark state-of-the-art LLVE and VOS methods on OLiVES and show that training on it improves performance on both tasks. The OLiVES project page is available at: https://anonymous-OLiVES.github.io/.

title: Hindsight-Privileged RLVR: Single-Rollout Token Credit Without Group Sampling
abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) trains language models from checked task outcomes, but assigning a terminal reward to individual reasoning tokens or actions remains difficult. Group-relative methods such as Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) sample several attempts per prompt, but lose their reward-based learning signal when all attempts receive the same outcome. We propose Hindsight-Privileged RLVR (HP-RLVR), a single-rollout method that turns a completed trajectory's own future into token-level update weights. The generating policy snapshot scores each eligible token under its causal history and under a hindsight context containing the realized future and verifier feedback. A normalized Jensen--Shannon divergence between the two views weights the reward relative to a historical baseline, yielding bounded token credit for both successful and failed attempts, with no reference solution or learned critic. In paired Qwen3-8B runs over a shared $100$-step schedule, HP-RLVR trains $1.21\times$, $1.46\times$, and $2.30\times$ faster than GRPO on mathematics, code generation, and ALFWorld, using one eighth the rollouts per prompt. Accuracy is comparable overall, with HP-RLVR ahead on mathematics at all three sizes and GRPO ahead on code and ALFWorld. In ALFWorld, $43.2\%$ (4B) and $49.0\%$ (8B) of GRPO's gradient-norm records are zero, versus none for HP-RLVR.

title: Quantifying privacy risks in foundation model representations of brain MRI
abstract: Pretrained representations are increasingly used to share and reuse information from medical images without exposing the original scans, but it is unclear how much patient-specific information these representations retain. We investigate this question for brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) by evaluating five frozen pretrained encoders spanning different architectures, pretraining objectives, and training domains on two longitudinal T1-weighted datasets, OASIS-2 and MIRIAD. Under an attacker model with access to released embeddings, the corresponding public encoder, and auxiliary MRI scans, we evaluate patient linkage and sensitive-attribute inference. Across the evaluated representations, we observe substantial subject-specific information: rank-1 patient linkage reaches up to 99\% on MIRIAD and exceeds 90\% on OASIS-2 for the highest-risk representation, despite the absence of an identification objective during encoder training. We further show that the released embeddings retain information about a demographic attribute, with recorded-sex prediction reaching balanced accuracy of 90.9\% on OASIS-2 and 95.5\% on MIRIAD. Overall, our results demonstrate that replacing raw brain MRI with learned embeddings does not, by itself, eliminate patient-linkage or attribute-inference risk, and is therefore insufficient on its own to establish anonymity.

title: Average-Reward Policy Identification from a Single Continuing Trajectory
abstract: In reinforcement learning, an agent must explore an unknown environment to learn how to make good decisions. Unlike methods that can freely sample any state--action pair, an agent learning from a single trajectory must spend additional time navigating between states. It is therefore natural to expect that learning from a single trajectory requires more experience. In this paper, we show that this additional cost is not always necessary. For average-reward reinforcement learning, we develop an algorithm that learns where to collect information while ensuring that the required samples can be obtained efficiently. We establish an upper bound on the number of interactions needed to identify a near-optimal policy. Furthermore, we prove a matching information theoretic lower bound, showing that, for a broad class of environments and at sufficiently high accuracy, learning from a single trajectory is no harder in the worst case than learning with unrestricted access to state action samples.
